message.content:
Here are some of the most popular and highly regarded sushi restaurants in Tokyo (in no particular order):

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights |
|------------|----------|------------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza | Legendary chef Jiro Ono; Michelin‑starred; famed for precision and quality. |
| **Sushi Saito** | Ginza | Three Michelin stars; intimate setting; renowned for buttery nigiri. |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza | Three Michelin stars; meticulous preparation; seasonal ingredients. |
| **Sushi Mizutani** | Ginza | Two Michelin stars; elegant, minimalist décor; fresh fish. |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Popular spot for fresh tuna; long lines but worth the wait. |
| **Sushi Daiwa** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Known for high‑quality sashimi and nigiri; often crowded. |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Ginza | Two Michelin stars; creative rolls and traditional nigiri. |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Ginza | Two Michelin stars; known for its “sashimi bar” concept. |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | Classic sushi experience; well‑known for its “Omakase” menu. |
| **Sushi Tsubaki** | Ginza | Two Michelin stars; emphasis on seasonal fish and subtle flavors. |
| **Sushi Shun** | Ginza | Two Michelin stars; known for its “Omakase” tasting menu. |
| **Sushi Kanda** | Ginza | Three Michelin stars; small, exclusive dining room. |

These spots range from ultra‑exclusive, Michelin‑starred establishments to more accessible market stalls that still deliver top‑tier sushi. Reservations are often required months in advance for the Michelin‑starred places, while the Tsukiji market stalls can be enjoyed on a first‑come, first‑served basis. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
